While the events in the story are entirely *appropriate* and believable within its grounded, realistic setting of academic bureaucracy, the narrative does not contain *surprising* turns or thrilling plot twists. The progression of the story—discovering a leak, enduring endless and botched construction phases, adapting to the disruption, and finally having the roof fixed—follows a very predictable, linear trajectory of institutional delay. Even the moment of "genuine peril" when water leaks into the archive room is immediately defused with the plain statement that "Nothing was lost," intentionally subverting dramatic tension in favor of quiet realism.
